title: Outage follow-up: we'll handle the customer emails
transcript:
[00:00] Sunil: Let's do the outage follow-up. Felix, what's the final count?
[00:06] Felix: Two hundred and twelve workspaces had sync paused for more than an hour over the weekend. Root cause was the queue migration. The rollback finished at 3:40.
[00:22] Imani: Support got about ninety tickets. Most were closed with the status page link, but around fifteen are still open and a couple are angry.
[00:35] Sunil: Are those fifteen inside the two hundred and twelve?
[00:40] Imani: I think so. I haven't cross-checked.
[00:45] Felix: I can export the affected workspace list with the owner emails.
[00:51] Sunil: Good. We agreed in the incident review that anyone down over an hour gets a credit. Is the credit applied automatically?
[01:01] Felix: Not yet. Billing needs a CSV. I'll have the credits applied by Thursday.
[01:09] Sunil: OK. And the affected customers need to hear from us directly, not just through the status page.
[01:17] Imani: Agreed. The ones with open tickets keep asking whether it'll happen again.
[01:24] Felix: The postmortem draft answers that. We added a canary for the queue and a migration lock.
[01:33] Sunil: Right. So we'll handle the customer emails by tomorrow. Plain language, the credit, and what we changed.
[01:42] Imani: Sounds good.
[01:44] Felix: Yep, makes sense.
[01:47] Sunil: Imani, can you also close out the open tickets once the email is out, pointing to it?
[01:54] Imani: Yes, I'll do that with a macro.
[01:58] Felix: I'll publish the postmortem on the blog after legal reads it.
[02:05] Sunil: Great. Anything else on the outage?
[02:09] Imani: Just that the status page went up twenty minutes late. We should look at that.
[02:16] Felix: That one's on the on-call checklist. I'll add a step for it.
[02:22] Sunil: Thanks, both.
